objective: Restore start:desktop on Windows PowerShell 5.1 by generating the existing 32-byte Minecraft session secret with a cross-version CSPRNG API.
non_goals: Do not change token size, encoding, authority, routes, ports, startup ordering or child-process ownership.
Do not expose the token to renderer, logs, files, command-line arguments or persisted configuration.
Do not change Minecraft skills, models, Vision, speech, avatar or resource scheduling.
contracts: Every Desktop session receives a fresh 32-byte cryptographically secure random Minecraft control secret.
The token remains URL-safe unpadded Base64 and exists only in the launcher and child-process environment boundary.
The CSPRNG object is disposed even if generation fails, and the previous environment value is restored on exit.
The exact production token helper executes successfully under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7-compatible .NET runtimes.
allowed_dependencies: Existing .NET System.Security.Cryptography APIs only; no new dependency.
acceptance_criteria: The reproduced RandomNumberGenerator.Fill MethodNotFound path is removed.
A regression test executes the exact production helper in Windows PowerShell and validates URL-safe encoding plus 32 decoded bytes without printing the secret.
Desktop tests, launcher startup smoke, module-brief validation, GitNexus detect_changes and git diff check pass.
required_test_commands: uv run --frozen python -c "import json; from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator; schema=json.load(open('docs/schemas/module-brief.schema.json', encoding='utf-8')); brief=json.load(open('docs/modules/M09-S6A-windows-powershell-token-hotfix-module-brief.json', encoding='utf-8')); Draft202012Validator(schema).validate(brief)"
